assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and realised to uncertainties near 1e-18, are a clear step change in precision measurement. They underpin redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants and dark-matter couplings. The concept is original, the lasting impact is broad and the experimental clarity is high.
assessment.attribution: Katori originated the magic-wavelength lattice-clock concept and first demonstrated it; Ye drove the record-accuracy strontium clocks and the link to frequency combs. Two names give a clean, defensible configuration. Other groups (e.g. Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow) made important contributions, and Ye's comb and ultrastable-laser work overlaps with the 2005 prize, but the lattice-clock credit is separable.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups worldwide have confirmed the approach for over a decade, with comparisons across continents and use in the roadmap to a new SI second. Timing is right, with no interpretive instability.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to wait for the formal SI redefinition.
Fair weight to other lattice-clock pioneers beyond two names; I rely on memory for the detailed priority history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies: discovery of a diffuse astrophysical flux in 2013, the TXS 0506+056 blazar association and evidence for the Galactic plane. It is a technically bold instrument, a km3 detector in Antarctic ice, and opens a new observational window, squarely in astroparticle physics.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and its predecessor AMANDA; Spiering was a founding figure of neutrino telescopes and spokesperson across the DUMAND/Baikal/AMANDA/IceCube lineage. Credit for such a large collaboration is inevitably diffuse and others (e.g. Learned, Goldhaber for Cherenkov-in-water concepts; Baikal pioneers) have claims. The two supplied names are the strongest fair pair. I note my own field is adjacent and I should apply the same standard as for others.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed by several analyses and by ANTARES/KM3NeT data of consistent character; source identification is still thin beyond one blazar and the Galactic plane. The detector is mature but the astrophysics of sources is still being developed.
uncertainties: Source identification of the diffuse flux remains incomplete.
Allocation among founders of neutrino-telescope technology is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP turned the CMB into a precision cosmological tool: acoustic peaks, the age of the universe, flat geometry, composition and reionization, establishing LambdaCDM with percent-level parameters. This is an exceptionally clear and lasting impact, building directly on COBE (2006) and the cosmological-parameter story that fed into 2011 and 2019 recognition.
assessment.attribution: Bennett was PI and led the mission and the core analysis, Page led the instrument and optics, and Spergel led the parameter interpretation and theory. This fits the three-person limit well and tracks distinct essential contributions. Planck and the broader team (Wilkinson, Hinshaw, Komatsu and others) also mattered, so a boundary is arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Results confirmed and strengthened independently by Planck, ACT and SPT. Timing is mature; the risk is that some committee members may see the key discovery as already honoured via COBE and the dark-energy prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with already-awarded cosmology prizes weighs against novelty.
Whether the committee sees the instrument-led credit assignment as sufficiently clean.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS completed the Standard Model and rested on a remarkable technical achievement in detector design, triggering and data analysis at the LHC. The impact is fundamental and lasting. The theory was recognised in 2013, so this addresses the experimental half.
assessment.attribution: Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee were the founding conceptual and project leaders of CMS and ATLAS (spokespersons and proponents). This is a defensible three-person configuration for instrument creation, but it is not the same as crediting the discovery analysis, which was made by thousands. Alternative configurations such as the 2012 spokespersons are conceivable. The Nobel statutes remain awkward for collaborations.
assessment.maturity: Two independent experiments and a decade of couplings measurements have confirmed the particle's properties. Timing is mature, and the instrument-building angle recognises design rather than a discovery moment, which is arguably well matched to the prize.
uncertainties: Whether recognising founders rather than discoverers is a fair and accepted reading of the discovery.
Unclear boundary with the wider collaboration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of X-ray afterglows with BeppoSAX followed by optical/radio counterparts and redshifts settled the long-standing question of the distance of gamma-ray bursts, showing they are cosmological and enormously energetic. This changed high-energy astrophysics and links to collapsars, GW170817 and relativistic jets.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX discovery of the X-ray afterglow in 1997; Kulkarni led optical and radio follow-up and redshift work. Others deserve mention (van Paradijs, Djorgovski, Metzger, Piro, Frail), and the optical-redshift credit is shared. The supplied three are a plausible set but not obviously unique.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by Swift, Fermi and many later bursts; the interpretation is stable. The discovery is nearly three decades old, so timing is late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Competing claims for the first optical afterglow and redshift.
Whether the Prize would be seen as for the discovery or the follow-up interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, with flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity, opened the field of moire quantum materials and twistronics. The originality is high: a tunable, clean platform for strong correlations with wide follow-on impact.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle and flat bands in 2011; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 observations of correlated insulating states and superconductivity. Cao and others are first authors on those papers, and Dean's and Young's work on moire systems is also relevant, so allocation is not trivial. Theory-plus-experiment is a natural Nobel pattern.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups, but the microscopic nature of the superconductivity and correlated phases is still debated and reproducibility has depended on sample quality. Somewhat early, though the field is active.
uncertainties: Whether the experimental credit should include other moire pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon microstrip and hybrid/3D pixel detectors enabled vertexing and tracking in modern collider experiments, making possible heavy-flavour tagging, the top quark, Higgs discovery and imaging in other fields. As an experimentalist I value instrument inventions that enable discoveries, and this has had lasting importance, though impact is as enabling technology rather than a single physical discovery.
assessment.attribution: Parker developed silicon microstrip and 3D detectors; Heijne pioneered the planar silicon detector and hybrid pixel concept at CERN, with Campbell leading the Medipix/hybrid pixel developments. Other pioneers (Kemmer, Rancoita, Hall, Dalla Betta, Rossi) shaped the field, so the allocation is not uniquely resolved.
assessment.maturity: The technology is mature, ubiquitous, and confirmed in decades of operation. Recognition is arguably overdue but the prize history on instruments is selective.
uncertainties: Credit boundaries across many institutional teams.
Whether the committee will weigh enabling instrumentation above a discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Event Horizon Telescope imaged the shadow of M87* and Sgr A* using global VLBI at 230 GHz, a direct demonstration of strong-field gravity at a horizon scale. It is a spectacular technical and scientific result, with high clarity for the public and the field.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow-imaging concept (with Melia and Agol) and Doeleman led the VLBI development and the EHT collaboration. Zensus and others, plus the imaging-algorithm teams, also played large roles. A configuration of two is possible but leaves out many contributors.
assessment.maturity: The images are 2019 and 2022; polarization and multi-epoch results are developing, and tests of GR are limited by resolution and modelling. A somewhat early moment, though an important validation.
uncertainties: Image reconstruction and interpretation are model dependent.
